flagship.headline: The Rolling Stones begin their Muscle Shoals sessions
flagship.summary_line_1: The Rolling Stones started a three-day session at Muscle Shoals Sound Studio in Sheffield, Alabama on December 2, 1969, and cut Brown Sugar on the first day, per American Songwriter.
flagship.summary_line_2: They stayed two more days and recorded Wild Horses and You Gotta Move, and the clip below is Brown Sugar, released on Sticky Fingers in 1971.

events.headline: The Rolling Stones begin their Muscle Shoals sessions
events.summary_line_1: The Rolling Stones started a three-day session at Muscle Shoals Sound Studio in Sheffield, Alabama on December 2, 1969, and cut Brown Sugar on the first day, per American Songwriter.
events.summary_line_2: They stayed two more days and recorded Wild Horses and You Gotta Move, and the clip below is Brown Sugar, released on Sticky Fingers in 1971.

events.headline: George Harrison joins Delaney & Bonnie on stage in Bristol
events.summary_line_1: George Harrison played with Delaney & Bonnie & Friends at Colston Hall in Bristol on December 2, 1969, the second date of their UK tour, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: It was his first stage appearance since the Beatles' last concert in 1966, he had agreed to join the tour the night before, and the clip below is Comin' Home, a Delaney & Bonnie single from 1969.

events.headline: Nate Mendel is born in Richland, Washington
events.summary_line_1: Bassist Nate Mendel was born in Richland, Washington on December 2, 1968, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: He went on to play bass in Sunny Day Real Estate and Foo Fighters, and the clip below is Everlong, a Foo Fighters single.

events.headline: The Monkees top both Billboard charts
events.summary_line_1: The Monkees held No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 with Daydream Believer in the chart dated December 2, 1967, the first of four weeks on top, per Billboard and Songfacts.
events.summary_line_2: Their album Pisces, Aquarius, Capricorn & Jones Ltd. reached No. 1 on the album chart the same week, and the clip below is Daydream Believer.

events.headline: David Bowie releases Rubber Band on Deram
events.summary_line_1: Deram released David Bowie's single Rubber Band in the UK on December 2, 1966, backed with The London Boys, per Bowie Bible.
events.summary_line_2: It failed to chart, like his other early singles, and the clip below is the song.

events.headline: The Beatles mix their fourth Christmas record
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles mixed and edited their fourth Christmas record, Pantomime: Everywhere It's Christmas, in Room 53 at EMI Studios in Abbey Road on December 2, 1966, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: They were recording Strawberry Fields Forever at Abbey Road in the same weeks, and the clip below is that single.

events.headline: The Rolling Stones play the Seattle Coliseum
events.summary_line_1: The Rolling Stones played the Seattle Coliseum on December 2, 1965, on their second American tour, per Wikipedia and a Seattle Times retrospective.
events.summary_line_2: The tour ran from October 29 to December 5, and the clip below is (I Can't Get No) Satisfaction, their 1965 hit.

events.headline: Ringo Starr has his tonsils removed
events.summary_line_1: Surgeons at University College Hospital in London removed Ringo Starr's tonsils on December 2, 1964, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: He had checked in the day before and left hospital on December 10, and the clip below is I Wanna Be Your Man, his lead vocal on With the Beatles.

events.headline: The Beatles tape The Morecambe and Wise Show
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles filmed an appearance on ATV's The Morecambe and Wise Show at the Elstree Studio Centre in Borehamwood on December 2, 1963, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: That night they played a concert in the ballroom of the Grosvenor House hotel in London, and the clip below is All My Loving, from their album released ten days earlier.

events.headline: The Beatles play two shows at the Embassy Cinema
events.summary_line_1: Brian Epstein got the Beatles onto the bill of Frank Ifield's two shows at the Embassy Cinema in Peterborough on December 2, 1962, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: Their debut single, Love Me Do, had come out that October, and the clip below is that single.

events.headline: Frank Sinatra plays Sydney Stadium
events.summary_line_1: Frank Sinatra performed at the Stadium in Sydney on December 2, 1961, filmed and recorded during his Australian visit, per thefranksinatra.com and Noise11.
events.summary_line_2: The concert survives on tape and is included in a later box set, and the clip below is Come Fly With Me, one of his best-known recordings.

events.headline: Rick Savage is born in Sheffield
events.summary_line_1: Rick Savage, the bassist and co-founder of Def Leppard, was born in Sheffield, England on December 2, 1960, per This Day in Music.
events.summary_line_2: He co-founded the band that became Def Leppard in 1977, and the clip below is Pour Some Sugar on Me.
